verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a community report that a user enabled macOS's built-in Remote Management on a second Mac and logged into it remotely via Remote Desktop. That suggests the OS can expose a desktop for remote access, but there is no first-party documentation of the feature. Adjacent features such as iPhone Mirroring, AirPlay to Mac, Sidecar and Universal Control are device-to-device or nearby-device features, not remote desktop sessions, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: first-party docs on Screen Sharing/Remote Management, evidence of acting as a client to remote desktop sessions (e.g., VNC/RDP), and setup, permissions or cross-network usage details.
